title: Ledger audit: corrections applied rigorously with sources
method: re-read every script+JSON claim touching alpha_cusp, the escape threshold, and the direction counts; verified each against the code's own MC/closed forms; corrected scripts, regenerated JSONs, and recorded every change here.  Key reconciliation: the escape rule I*h/X > g0*gdepth*d* (=0.1266) is equivalent to h/X > theta_star = g0*gdepth*d*/I = 0.0633, and theta_star = g0*gdepth*alpha_cusp where alpha_cusp = (g*-g0)/(I*g0*gdepth) = d*/I = 1.0553 is a DIMENSIONLESS g-axis marker at the phase cusp g*, not an h/X threshold.

standing_withdrawals_unchanged: genesis_relaxation.json: Yang-Mills-style spectral-mass-gap reading withdrawn (linear sector gapless); |lambda|=0.0883 is a rotation modulus, not a relaxation rate.
genesis_law.json: 'log-uniform (Jeffreys)' threat spectrum withdrawn (was a Jacobian bug); corrected density is Pareto-2 in the main band.
genesis_euler.json / genesis_tail.json: no pi/e/i numeric miracle claimed; alpha~pi/3 is a chance-level hit under 96 comparisons.

genesis_overshoot.json: the 'gate meets account / trust drains to zero' mechanism for the g0 dependence of the overshoot is WITHDRAWN.  Probe showed trust at denial is healthy (234..365, well above 0) and depth-at-denial is quasi-stable ~0.8 for both g0; doubling g0 floods the denial RATE (1668 -> 10818) at similar depth.  The g0 effect on the overshoot is a denial-rate effect, not a gate-collapse.  Also NOT claimed: the fitted constant C=2.25 (no mechanism) and the single-step closed form eps = X(1+g(d)L) - floor*L (matches baseline ~1.39 vs -1.56 within draw spread but FAILS g0x2: pred 1.52 vs measured -0.74).  Verified surviving facts: U = X + eps identity to machine precision; eps scales with draw magnitude; flat in floor/n; seed-stable.

genesis_denial_rate.json: the earlier '6.5x per g0-doubling, power 2.7' flood reading (from the genesis_overshoot mechanism probe, 1668 -> 10818) is WITHDRAWN as a HORIZON ARTIFACT.  The denial rate is NON-STATIONARY: per-window rate at low g0 (0.06) ramps monotonically without settling across 3000 steps (0.0046,0.0176,0.0225,0.0286,0.0302,0.0407; last/first 8.85) - a slow first-passage penetration, not burn-in; at high g0 (0.15) it saturates after a transient to a plateau ~0.13 (0.018,0.169,0.176,0.122,0.128,0.137).  There is NO single steady-state denial rate at marginal drawdown.  Claimed invariants only: identity U=X+eps (machine precision), overshoot scales with draw / flat in floor & n / seed-stable, and quasi-stable gate depth ~0.8.
standing_refinements_epistemic: genesis_overshoot / genesis_denial_rate earlier called the gate depth 'quasi-stable ~0.8'.  Depth-pinning census (genesis_depthpin.json) REFINES this: depth@den is only WEAKLY pinned and is NOT a universal constant.  It is near-pinned (~0.7-0.8) against the ECONOMIC-PRESSURE knobs (draw scale 8x: 0.70->0.78; g0 x2: 0.82) while the OVERSHOOT absorbs their response (~4x) - but the REGENERATION knob n moves DEPTH (n x5: 0.8->0.99 toward full leverage), and floor x100 lowers it (0.75).  So the honest law is DIFFERENTIAL: economic-pressure -> overshoot; regeneration (n/floor) -> depth.  The n knob alone can unpin the refusal depth toward the nominal leverage 1.0.

genesis_trip.json refines the overshoot further: leverage denial is a THRESHOLD-triggered measure, not a linear compliance.  My own earlier 'compliance 0.475/tick in n' reading is WITHDRAWN as an EMPTY-LOW-END-SAMPLE artifact (at small draws there were ZERO leverage denials, so both end-points trivially agreed at 0.000).  Corrected: when a big draw trips the leverage gate, eps = -(credit)-trust at that moment is ~ -1.42, INVARIANT under n (0.10, 0.50) and moderate floor (0.001); only a 100x floor (0.10) shifts it (eps -> -1.73, denials 10888 -> 4347).  Differential holds: n moves DEPTH (0.8 -> 0.99) but leaves eps@trip ~ -1.42; floor moves both.  -1.42 is a measured threshold at this parameter point, not a universal constant.

genesis_trip_geometry.json CLOSES the arc: eps@trip is a function of the g(d)=g0(1+gdepth*d) GEOMETRY pair only (decoupled from the regeneration sector).  gdepth sweep (g0=0.05): eps@trip -1.601,-1.487,-1.424,-1.249,-1.129 for gdepth 0.5,1.0,1.2,2.0,3.0 - MONOTONE (steeper depth-progressive drawdown pulls the gross gate inward, less overshoot).  g0 sweep (gdepth=1.2): -1.698,-1.424,-1.310,-1.146,-1.104,-1.099,-1.139,-1.191 for g0 0.025..0.20 - NON-MONOTONIC with an INTERIOR OPTIMUM near g0 ~ 0.12 (largest overshoot suppression); too-small g0 leaves large overshoot, too-large slightly reinflates.  So: optimal drawdown rate exists (~0.12 at gdepth=1.2); 'bigger g' is not monotonically better.  No simple closed form, no fitted constant, no numeric miracle claimed.  SEED-ROBUSTNESS CONFIRMED: the interior optimum is at g0=0.12 in seeds 7/2/99 (eps@opt -1.099, -0.958, -1.042; magnitude spread ~0.15) with the dip-then-reinflate shape identical in all - so the optimum is a law of LOCATION/SHAPE, not a tuned value.

genesis_trip_mechanism.json EXPLAINS the g0 optimum's cause (turning the law into an understood one).  Measured (seed 7): median trust@trip 236.9->23.5->3.7->0.2->0.1->0.01 as g0 goes 0.025->0.30, and frac of denials at depth>1.2 is 0.0000 for g0<=0.12 (the optimum) but jumps to ~0.05 for g0>0.12.  Mechanism: g(d) collapses trust to near-zero above the optimum, and since depth = |credit|/trust, the depth DIVERGES via a VANISHING DENOMINATOR as trust->0, producing a deep-denial tail that reinflates the overshoot.  So the optimum (~0.12) is the LARGEST drawdown that still keeps ALL denials at finite full-leverage-like depth with not-yet-collapsed trust.  Robust claim is the MECHANISM (vanishing-trust divergence), not the optimum's numerical location.

genesis_trip_mechanism.json PHASE-BOUNDARY ROBUSTNESS: the deep-tail onset (frac of leverage denials at depth>1.2 rising from exactly 0.000 at g0<=0.12 to 2-6% at g0>=0.14) is a SHARP PHASE BOUNDARY in g0 located at g0 ~ 0.12-0.14, UNIVERSAL across gdepth (0.8,1.2,2.0) and seed (7,99) - all 6 cells show 0.000 then a jump - and it always coincides with the median-trust collapse at trip (e.g. gdepth=1.2 seed=7: trust 23.5 -> 0.8 -> 0.1 as g0 goes 0.10->0.14->0.15).  So the trust-collapse/vanishing-denominator mechanism is a structural phase transition, not a tuned point; its LOCATION (~0.12-0.14 at these params) is parameter-point, its ONSET STRUCTURE is robust.

genesis_trip_mechanism.json tests whether the phase boundary is a g0-alone control or a g0*gdepth product (i.e. whether the operating-depth drawdown g(d)=g0(1+gdepth*d) is the variable).  RESULT: the fine onset is essentially constant in g0 (~0.135-0.140) across gdepth 0.6-3.0, while both multiplicative candidates vary ~2-5x (g0(1+0.8gdepth): 0.2072->0.4590; g0*gdepth: 0.084->0.405).  So the boundary is in g0 ALONE - gdepth is inert (only ~4% drift) - a near-VERTICAL phase line in the (g0,gdepth) plane.  This REFINES the earlier 'geometry pair' framing: the pair sets the trip-overshoot MAGNITUDE, but the trust-collapse PHASE BOUNDARY is controlled by the base drawdown rate g0 alone.  Governance: tuning gdepth does not move the refusal-collapse boundary; only g0 does.
